question: If you discover a defect that could affect the safe operation of your vehicle, you should:
options: a:Delay fixing it until you can afford repairs.,b:Drive at slower speeds until it can be fixed.,c:Correct the defect as soon as possible.
note: Any defect that affects safe vehicle operation should be repaired promptly and before driving when possible.

question: To be prepared for what lies ahead on the roadway, you should:
options: a:Stare straight ahead at all times.,b:Continually scan the entire roadway and roadsides.,c:Drive with your left foot lightly resting on the brake.
note: Search the road and sides continually to identify hazards early; do not simply stare at the center of the road.

question: You must yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles when:
options: a:Only when other vehicles yield,b:Under no circumstances.,c:You see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
note: Yield the right-of-way immediately to any emergency vehicle using lights or sirens by pulling over to the curb and stopping.

question: Drowsy drivers:
options: a:Can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.,b:Can drive so poorly they may appear to be drunk.,c:Should drink strong coffee to remain alert.
note: Drowsiness can severely impair driving ability; coffee, open windows, or loud radios are not reliable remedies.

question: If you must stop along the road at night, what should you do with your lights?
options: a:Leave your low-beam headlights on (and use emergency flashers),b:Turn off all your lights,c:Use only your parking lights
note: If you stop at night, use your emergency flashers and keep low-beam headlights on so other drivers can see your vehicle clearly.

question: When driving in fog you should use:
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow so you are better able to see and be seen.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:Only when exiting an expressway.,b:Only when following a motorcycle.,c:When behind a large vehicle that blocks your view or in bad weather.
note: Increase following distance in many situations: large vehicles that block vision, bad weather, heavy traffic, or if tailgated.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you're stopped in line at a stop sign and there is no cross traffic after vehicles ahead have passed, what must you do?
options: a:Proceed without stopping because the way is clear.,b:Stop again at the stop sign or stop line before proceeding.,c:Slowly roll past the stop sign.
note: You must always come to a complete stop at the stop sign and yield before proceeding, even if vehicles ahead have moved.

question: Many crashes are caused by drivers who:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way.,b:Travel too fast for the conditions.,c:Constantly check their mirrors.
note: Driving too quickly for road or weather conditions is a common factor in crashes.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim high beams, where should you direct your gaze?
options: a:At the lights of the approaching vehicle.,b:Toward the right side of the road.,c:Toward the left side of the road.
note: Glance to the right side of the road to avoid being blinded while keeping enough sight to stay on course.

question: Which statement best defines defensive driving?
options: a:Defensive driving means defending yourself by getting ahead of bad drivers in traffic.,b:Defensive driving means following the vehicle ahead of you at a close distance.,c:Defensive driving means identifying dangerous situations and taking action to avoid accidents.
note: Defensive driving is recognizing hazards early and taking action to avoid collisions, reducing conflicts with aggressive or inattentive road users.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which steps should you take when changing lanes on a highway?
options: a:Signal, check rearview and side mirrors, then glance over your shoulder to check blind spots.,b:Only signal if there is visible traffic behind you.,c:Just check your mirrors and change lanes quickly.
note: Before changing lanes, signal, check mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to verify blind spots are clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following has authority over the others and must be obeyed first?
options: a:A stop sign,b:A police officer,c:A steady red light
note: Directions given by a police officer or other authorized traffic officer take precedence over traffic signals, signs, or pavement markings.

question: Which of the following is a common sign of a drunk driver?
options: a:Weaving between lanes and making sudden,b:Always driving faster than traffic.,c:Consistently maintaining perfect lane position.
note: Signs of impairment include weaving, erratic speed changes, jerking motions, and sudden stops.

question: Alcoholic beverages can affect you by:
options: a:Improving thinking ability.,b:Slowing your reaction time.,c:Giving you increased
note: Alcohol impairs reaction time, judgment, balance, and vision while giving false confidence.

question: What do work zone (orange) signs indicate?
options: a:That it is summer and roads are busier.,b:Less-than-ideal driving conditions and that construction or maintenance is present.,c:You must immediately stop and back up.
note: Orange work zone signs warn drivers of road work; slow down and be extra cautious.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing that has no gates or flashing lights, you should:
options: a:Cross the tracks immediately and as quickly as possible.,b:Always stop before crossing no matter what.,c:Prepare to yield to any train that may be approaching.
note: If there are no active signals, be prepared to yield and only cross when there is room for your entire vehicle on the other side and you are sure no trains are coming.

question: On a divided multilane highway when you hear or see an emergency vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down,b:Disregard the signal if other lanes are available.,c:Stop as quickly as possible wherever you are.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches, slow down and make a clear path by moving and stopping when safe; do not try to outdrive the vehicle.

question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing without signals?
options: a:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,b:Always come to a complete stop.,c:Assume there will always be signals.
note: At an un-signaled railroad crossing slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop if a train is approaching.

question: In foggy conditions you should:
options: a:Use your high beams to see farther ahead.,b:Use parking lights only.,c:Drive cautiously
note: Fog reduces visibility; use low beams (and fog lights if equipped), slow down, and increase following distance.

question: When approaching a stopped school bus on the opposite side of a divided highway, what must drivers do?
options: a:Must stop until the stop arm is lifted regardless of division.,b:Must stop until the bus begins moving.,c:May continue driving if the highway is divided.
note: If the highway is divided by a median or barrier, drivers on the opposite side may continue; otherwise all lanes must stop for a stopped school bus with its signals activated.

question: How does the type of alcoholic drink affect impairment?
options: a:Wine impairs less than beer.,b:Beer impairs less than wine.,c:The effect on reflexes and judgment depends on blood alcohol level
note: Impairment depends on the amount of alcohol in the bloodstream, not whether it comes from beer, wine, or spirits.

question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you on a two-lane, two-way road, you should:
options: a:Pull off to the right side of the road and let traffic pass.,b:Decrease your speed further.,c:Refuse to let other cars pass your vehicle.
note: Driving significantly slower than the flow of traffic is hazardous. On a two-lane road you must pull off and let vehicles pass when it is safe to do so.

question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes of traffic mean?
options: a:Traffic in the lanes moves in opposite directions.,b:Drivers may pass or change lanes when it is safe to do so.,c:Drivers may not pass in this area.
note: Dashed white lines separate lanes going in the same direction and may be crossed to pass or change lanes when it is safe.

question: Alcohol consumption commonly causes:
options: a:Loss of concentration.,b:Only slower judgment.,c:Only poor coordination.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol impair vision, concentration, judgment, and coordination.

question: A good defensive driver:
options: a:Always drives slowly.,b:Maintains a constant speed at all times.,c:Anticipates and watches for other drivers' actions.
note: Defensive drivers look ahead, anticipate others' actions, and prepare for potential hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left onto a one-way street, you should complete the turn into:
options: a:The lane closest to your previous lane.,b:Either lane of the one-way street.,c:The right lane of the one-way street.
note: Turn from the lane nearest the direction you are traveling into the lane nearest the direction you want to go on the one-way street.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:A vehicle may proceed without stopping.,b:The vehicle that arrived first.,c:The vehicle that arrived last.
note: At a four-way stop the driver who arrived first should proceed first. If two arrive simultaneously, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

question: When backing a vehicle, you should:
options: a:Open your door to see if it is safe to proceed.,b:Rely only on your mirrors,c:Turn and look through the rear window while backing rather than relying only on mirrors.
note: When reversing, turn and look over your shoulder through the rear window; do not depend solely on mirrors or sensors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, what should you do first?
options: a:Re-enter your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.,b:Honk at the vehicle three times to warn them.,c:Check mirrors and blind spots
note: Check mirrors and blind spots, signal your intent, pass safely, then return to the lane when you can see the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, how should you position your front wheels?
options: a:Turn the wheels to the right toward the curb.,b:Turn the wheels to the left away from the curb.,c:Keep the wheels straight ahead.
note: When parked downhill on a two-way street, turn front wheels toward the curb so the vehicle will roll into the curb rather than into traffic if it moves.

question: Which statement about passing a motorcycle is correct?
options: a:The driver of a passenger vehicle must change lanes completely when passing a motorcycle.,b:It is okay for other vehicles to follow motorcycles closely.,c:A motorcycle with two people is always more balanced than one with a single rider.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane; change lanes completely when passing to provide adequate space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on a freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Make a U-turn across the median.,b:Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.,c:Continue to the next exit and leave there.
note: If you miss an exit, drive to the next one; do not stop, back up, or cross the median on the freeway.

question: If another vehicle is tailgating you, what should you do first if there is an open lane to your right?
options: a:Move over to the right,b:Never slow down abruptly.,c:If there is not an open lane to your right
note: If someone is tailgating, move over to the right when it is safe to let them pass. If no lane is available, reduce speed gradually to encourage them to go around; avoid sudden braking.

question: Drivers who have been drinking before getting behind the wheel:
options: a:Are always aware of the risks they are taking.,b:Are better drivers because they are more careful than sober drivers.,c:Do not have sufficient control over their bodies and minds or the vehicles being driven.
note: Alcohol impairs judgment, vision, reaction time, and coordination; it is never safe to drive after drinking.

question: A leaking exhaust system can produce which dangerous effect?
options: a:Require more frequent oil changes.,b:Make you drowsy while driving and expose you to toxic fumes.,c:Reduce engine overheating only.
note: Leaky exhaust can let toxic gases into the vehicle, causing drowsiness, unconsciousness, or death in short order.

question: Which statement about driving on wet roadways is true?
options: a:The faster you drive,b:Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.,c:Water does not affect cars with good tires.
note: At higher speeds tires may lose contact with the road surface and the vehicle can hydroplane.

question: What does a single broken white line down the center of a multi-lane road indicate?
options: a:Lanes are moving in the same direction and passing is never allowed.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and passing is prohibited.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers may change lanes when safe.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction; you may change lanes when safe to do so.

question: If an emergency vehicle is approaching with lights and siren, you must:
options: a:Only pull over if the emergency vehicle is behind you.,b:Continue driving if you are going faster than the emergency vehicle.,c:Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop
note: You must pull to the right and stop to allow emergency vehicles to pass, whether they approach from behind or in the opposite direction.

question: How can you avoid alcohol-related crashes?
options: a:Say No thanks,b:Rely on coffee to sober up.,c:Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive.
note: The only reliable way to avoid drunk driving is to decide not to drive before drinking; alcohol impairs judgment.

question: A flashing yellow traffic signal indicates you should:
options: a:Come to a complete stop.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Turn on your headlights.
note: A flashing yellow light warns of a hazard; reduce speed and proceed carefully.

question: If you are involved in a crash and your vehicle is blocking traffic, you should:
options: a:Move your vehicle off the traveled portion of the roadway,b:Wait for police before moving your vehicle.,c:Not move your vehicle under any circumstances.
note: After a minor collision, move vehicles off the roadway if you can. Do not leave the scene without giving information and rendering assistance if needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a \No stopping\" sign generally allow you to do?"
options: a:Stop briefly to discharge passengers.,b:Stop to unload packages at any time.,c:Stop only to obey a traffic signal
note: A No Stopping sign permits stopping only to obey signals or officers or to avoid conflict with traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What greatly increases stopping distances and crash severity?
options: a:Slow speeds.,b:Night driving.,c:High speeds.
note: Higher speeds increase stopping distances and the force of impact in a collision.

question: Which of the following is true about sudden changes in weather and driving?
options: a:A sudden change in weather calls for an adjustment in your driving.,b:You should always slow down in rain and fog.,c:Be particularly aware of vehicles behind you only in inclement weather.
note: If weather changes suddenly, adjust your driving. Always slow down in rain or fog and be especially aware of vehicles behind you.

question: What shape/color denotes a slow-moving vehicle emblem?
options: a:A circular green sign.,b:A reflective orange triangle.,c:A rectangular red sign.
note: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle indicating a vehicle traveling 25 mph or less.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Driving significantly below the normal flow of traffic is:
options: a:Illegal.,b:Safe.,c:Smart.
note: Driving far slower than the normal speed of traffic is hazardous and, under ideal conditions, may be against the law.

question: If another driver cuts you off, what's the safest response?
options: a:Pull next to them and yell.,b:Let it go and continue driving safely.,c:Flash your high beams at them.
note: Avoid road rage by not taking aggressive actions; let it go and remain calm to continue driving safely.

question: When you encounter a sign saying “Reduced speed, 35 mph,” what does it mean?
options: a:The new 35 mph speed limit begins at that sign.,b:You have plenty of distance before the reduced zone starts.,c:The reduced speed begins at the next sign.
note: Reduced speed signs indicate the new speed limit takes effect at the location of the sign unless otherwise posted.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving in traffic, what speed strategy is safest?
options: a:Drive faster than the flow to avoid being hit,b:Drive with the flow of traffic within the posted limits.,c:Drive significantly slower than other vehicles.
note: Driving at the speed of traffic (within posted limits) reduces crash risk associated with speed differences.

question: Your vehicle's brake lights inform other drivers that you:
options: a:Have your emergency brake on.,b:Are making a turn.,c:Are slowing down or stopping.
note: Brake lights indicate to drivers behind you that you are slowing or stopping and should be in working order.

question: Which factors influence alcohol's effects on a person?
options: a:Only the amount of alcohol consumed.,b:Only the person's tolerance level.,c:Amount of food in the stomach
note: BAC is affected by how much you drink, how quickly, your weight, and whether you've eaten, among other factors.

question: At light rail intersections, what should you always do?
options: a:Drive around lowered crossing gates if no train is visible.,b:Assume trains will stop for you.,c:Pay attention
note: Obey signs and signals at rail crossings, look both ways, and never drive around lowered gates.

question: If you approach a railroad crossing with flashing warning lights, you should:
options: a:Stop no closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail and look for a train.,b:Slow down and look for a train before crossing.,c:Look for a train
note: When lights are flashing you must stop at a safe distance (no closer than 15 feet) and wait for the train to pass and signals to cease before crossing.

question: When parking uphill next to a curb, you should set the parking brake and:
options: a:Keep the front tires straight ahead.,b:Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.,c:Keep the rear tires against the curb.
note: When parking uphill on a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb so that if the vehicle rolls, it will roll into the curb rather than into traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the traffic light changes from green to yellow as you approach an intersection, you should:
options: a:Brake sharply to stop immediately in the center of the intersection.,b:Be prepared to stop safely.,c:Speed up to beat the red light.
note: A yellow light warns that the signal will soon turn red; slow down and stop if you can do so safely.

question: Passing is prohibited within how many feet of a railroad crossing?
options: a:200 feet,b:500 feet,c:100 feet
note: You may not pass other vehicles within 100 feet of a railroad crossing to ensure visibility and safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you are approaching a heavy truck from behind while going uphill, which is true?
options: a:You may not be able to legally pass the truck.,b:You may not be able to safely pass the truck.,c:The truck may be traveling at a speed slower than the posted speed limit.
note: Large vehicles often travel more slowly when climbing grades. On hills with limited visibility it may also be unsafe or unlawful to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How close may you legally follow a fire truck that is responding to an emergency?
options: a:You may follow as close as 750 feet.,b:You may follow as close as one block.,c:You must not follow closer than 500 feet.
note: Maintain at least 500 feet distance behind an emergency vehicle responding to an emergency; do not park within a block of where it has stopped.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless posted otherwise, what is the maximum speed limit in a business district?
options: a:30 mph.,b:55 mph.,c:40 mph.
note: The default speed limit in business districts is 30 mph unless signs indicate otherwise.

question: How do you check your blind spot when changing lanes to the left?
options: a:Rely only on your side mirror.,b:Glance over your right shoulder.,c:Glance over your left shoulder.
note: To check your blind spot when moving left, glance over your left shoulder to confirm no vehicle is beside you.

question: What is your blind spot?
options: a:The area you see in your rearview mirror.,b:An area you cannot see without moving your head.,c:The area directly behind your vehicle that's visible without turning.
note: Blind spots are areas alongside or behind your vehicle that you cannot see in mirrors and require a head turn to check.

question: When meeting a car with high beams on that blind you, what should you do?
options: a:Look toward the right edge of the road until the vehicle passes.,b:Speed up to get past the glare quickly.,c:Use your bright lights until they dim theirs.
note: Look to the right side of the road to avoid being blinded by oncoming high beams.

question: What is the safe method for crossing a railroad track?
options: a:Cross quickly if a train appears to be approaching.,b:Look both ways only if the red light is flashing.,c:Look and listen both ways
note: Before crossing tracks, always look and listen for trains and obey any signals or gates; never try to cross if a train is approaching.

question: Before entering a roundabout you must slow down and yield to whom?
options: a:Only vehicles in the roundabout.,b:Only bicyclists.,c:Vehicles
note: Yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout before entering.

question: Which of these is NOT an effect of drinking?
options: a:Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.,b:You are less alert.,c:Your judgment of speed and distance becomes more accurate.
note: Alcohol reduces alertness, slows reaction time, and distorts judgment of speed and distance.

question: If stopped at a railroad crossing with multiple tracks, when should you proceed?
options: a:Wait until you have a clear view of all tracks before moving.,b:Stop on the first track and then creep forward to check the next.,c:Proceed as soon as the first train passes.
note: Do not proceed until you can see clearly down all tracks; another train may be coming on a different track.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you return to your lane after passing another vehicle?
options: a:When the other vehicle signals you to return.,b:When you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,c:When you are directly next to the vehicle.
note: Return to your lane after passing when you can see the entire passed vehicle in your rearview mirror and it is safe to do so.

question: When should you always use your turn signal?
options: a:Only when turning left.,b:Only when other traffic is present.,c:Changing lanes
note: Use signals whenever changing lanes, entering or exiting parking spaces, or entering traffic from driveways, alleys, or parking areas.

question: If the driver ahead is distracted (one hand and talking), how should you respond?
options: a:Cut in front of them to avoid being behind a distracted driver.,b:Follow their example and drive similarly.,c:Give the vehicle extra space because its driver has a reduced safety margin.
note: Allow extra space around distracted drivers since their inattentiveness increases crash risk.

question: If your vehicle lacks ABS and you need to stop quickly, what should you do?
options: a:Lightly tap the brakes.,b:Hold down the brake pedal steady.,c:Firmly pump the brakes.
note: For vehicles without ABS, pumping the brakes helps stop quickly while retaining steering control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you approach a steady red traffic light you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop.,b:Drive through if there is no crossing traffic.,c:Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
note: A steady red light requires a complete stop. You may turn right on red only if not prohibited and the turn can be made safely.

question: How often must motor vehicles be inspected in New Hampshire?
options: a:Once every four years.,b:Once every two years.,c:Once a year during the owner's birth month.
note: Vehicles must be inspected annually during the owner's birth month at an official inspection station.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must stop at an intersection when you see which signal?
options: a:A steady yellow light.,b:A yellow arrow.,c:A flashing red light.
note: A flashing red light requires a complete stop, yielding to traffic and pedestrians before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should drivers treat a flashing red traffic light?
options: a:Continue because you have the right-of-way.,b:As a stop sign — stop,c:Drive through if no other cars are present.
note: Flashing red lights indicate a dangerous intersection and must be treated like a stop sign.

question: Who is required by law to wear a seat belt in a moving vehicle?
options: a:Anyone under the age of 18.,b:Only adult passengers.,c:Only the driver.
note: Anyone under 18 is required by law to be properly restrained; however, everyone is encouraged to wear seat belts.

question: Which of the following is true about crosswalks?
options: a:They are always indicated by vertical pavement markings only.,b:They exist whether or not they are marked,c:They are always marked by horizontal pavement markings.
note: Crosswalks may be marked or unmarked; drivers must stop to allow pedestrians to cross.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle on a two-lane road you should:
options: a:Return to the driving lane when there is enough room between you and the passed vehicle.,b:Remain in the left lane if you intend to turn left.,c:Return immediately to the right side of the roadway.
note: You should re-enter the right lane only when you can do so safely, leaving adequate space between you and the passed vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a narrow road where you meet an oncoming vehicle, you must:
options: a:Allow the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road.,b:Pull completely off the road and stop.,c:Demand the other vehicle pull over to make room.
note: On narrow roads both vehicles should leave at least one-half of the main-traveled portion so they can pass safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver may legally pass another vehicle on the right when:
options: a:It requires driving off the pavement.,b:On a narrow bridge.,c:The vehicle ahead is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane.
note: You may pass on the right if the vehicle ahead is turning left and there is a safe, legal lane to use.

question: How is drinking alcohol and driving characterized in terms of traffic safety?
options: a:A minor traffic safety problem.,b:Safe if you have only had a few drinks.,c:A serious traffic safety problem.
note: Driving while impaired by alcohol or drugs is a serious safety hazard and greatly increases the risk of crashes and injuries.

question: Traffic signs and pavement markings must be:
options: a:Considered mere suggestions.,b:Followed only when other traffic is present,c:Always obeyed.
note: Signs, signals, and pavement markings regulate traffic flow and must be obeyed to ensure safety on the road.

question: Where are roads more likely to freeze first?
options: a:On open,b:Only on hills or curves.,c:In shaded areas such as under trees or near buildings.
note: Shaded sections of roadway freeze more quickly and remain icy longer than sunlit areas; take extra care in shaded sections.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Into which lane should you turn when making a turn?
options: a:Into any lane available regardless of direction.,b:Into the lane farthest from your direction of travel.,c:Into the first available legal lane in the direction you're traveling.
note: Turn into the first legal lane to avoid crossing multiple lanes and reduce collision risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a street from a driveway, what must you do?
options: a:Drive slowly and expect others to get out of your way.,b:Honk to warn approaching vehicles and proceed.,c:Stop before the sidewalk and proceed only when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
note: Always stop before entering the roadway from a driveway, yield to pedestrians and approaching traffic, and cross the sidewalk area safely.

question: When you hear a fire engine's siren behind you, you must:
options: a:Drive with your hazard flashers on.,b:Slow down until it passes,c:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle is approaching with sirens, pull to the curb or side of the road and stop to allow it to pass.

question: Smoking or preparing to smoke while driving is:
options: a:Not affecting driving abilities.,b:Helpful to maintain driver alertness.,c:A distracting activity.
note: Smoking can require drivers to take hands off the wheel or eyes off the road, creating dangerous distractions.

question: Which of these is not a factor in stopping distance?
options: a:Braking distance.,b:Steering ability.,c:Reaction distance.
note: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance, not on steering ability.

question: To help avoid fatigue on a long trip it is a good idea to:
options: a:Drive with one eye open at a time.,b:Do arm exercises every hour.,c:Stop and rest every two hours.
note: Make regular stops to rest and stretch; if drowsy, stop driving and rest.

question: Lanes moving in the same direction are divided by which color lines?
options: a:Yellow lines.,b:Red lines.,c:White lines.
note: White lines separate lanes traveling in the same direction; yellow lines separate opposing traffic.

question: What is the most common color of warning signs?
options: a:Green.,b:Red.,c:Yellow with black markings.
note: Warning signs are usually diamond-shaped and yellow with black symbols or words to indicate hazards ahead.

question: A flashing yellow traffic signal tells drivers to:
options: a:Expect merging traffic only.,b:Stop for pedestrians.,c:Proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow signal means you should slow down and proceed with caution through the intersection.

question: Approximately how far might a fully loaded tractor-trailer need to stop from 55 mph?
options: a:About 50 feet.,b:About 125 feet.,c:About 400 feet.
note: Heavy trucks require significantly longer stopping distances than cars; a fully loaded tractor-trailer may need nearly 400 feet to stop from 55 mph.

question: What is a 'No zone'?
options: a:A one-way traffic area,b:A designated no passing zone,c:The blind spot area around a large commercial vehicle.
note: No zones are the large blind spots around trucks and buses where smaller vehicles disappear from the driver's view; avoid lingering there.

question: When driving to an unfamiliar place, the best preparation is to:
options: a:Drive with only a general idea of where you are going.,b:Plan your route in advance.,c:Depend on road signs to find your way
note: Plan your trip ahead of time and consult a map or directions so you are not distracted while driving in an unfamiliar area.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Signaling your intentions before turning or changing lanes is:
options: a:Required by law and a good driving habit.,b:Necessary only if other traffic is present.,c:Necessary only during the maneuver
note: You must signal in advance (at least 100 feet on most roads) to inform other road users of your intentions.

question: When is sounding your horn appropriate?
options: a:When you see a child who is about to run into the street.,b:Whenever you are passing a bicyclist.,c:While you are traveling through an intersection
note: Use the horn as a warning to prevent a crash or to alert someone who may not see you (for example, a child stepping into the street).

question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:Only when you see a police car.,b:When entering a highway with other cars.,c:Whenever conditions such as weather or visibility make driving less than perfect.
note: Reduce speed below the posted limit when road conditions, visibility, or weather make the posted speed unsafe.

question: If two railroad tracks run next to each other, after one train passes you should:
options: a:Always stop before crossing even if no trains are visible.,b:Assume it is safe to proceed because one train has passed.,c:Look for another train approaching on the other track before proceeding.
note: When parallel tracks are present, one train may pass while another is approaching on the adjacent track; wait until you are sure no trains are coming.

question: What is the only effective way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Drink coffee to sober up quickly.,b:Exercise to reduce BAC.,c:Allow your body time to metabolize the alcohol.
note: Only time allows your body to metabolize alcohol. Coffee, exercise, or cold showers do not reduce BAC or make you sober.

question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, you should turn your front wheels:
options: a:Slightly to the right.,b:Sharply toward the curb.,c:Sharply away from the curb.
note: To prevent your vehicle from rolling into traffic when parked uphill, turn wheels sharply away from the curb.

question: On slippery roads, you should take turns and curves:
options: a:More quickly to clear the hazard faster.,b:At the same speed as usual.,c:More slowly than you would under normal conditions.
note: Reduce your speed before entering curves on slippery surfaces to maintain control and avoid skidding.

question: What is your first action if your accelerator sticks while driving?
options: a:Shift to neutral and apply steady pressure to the brakes.,b:Reach down and attempt to pull it up.,c:Shift to park immediately.
note: If the accelerator sticks, keep eyes on the road, shift into neutral, apply steady braking, pull safely off the road, and turn off the engine.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an intersection ahead is blocked by traffic you should:
options: a:Go slowly until the traffic ahead moves.,b:Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through without stopping.,c:Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can completely clear it; blocking intersections impedes traffic flow and is unsafe.

question: What is the most important rule for managing speed in curves?
options: a:Maintain the posted speed limit entering the curve and brake only in the sharpest part.,b:Accelerate gently before entering the curve.,c:Slow down before you enter the curve.
note: Because inertia can push you outward in a curve, reduce speed before entering to maintain control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when you come to an intersection with a flashing red light?
options: a:Slow down but do not stop.,b:Proceed without stopping if no other cars are present.,c:Come to a full stop and go only when it is safe.
note: A flashing red light has the same meaning as a stop sign: stop, yield right-of-way, then proceed when safe.

question: You may not park within how many feet of a crosswalk at an intersection?
options: a:20 feet.,b:10 feet.,c:30 feet.
note: Drivers may not park within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection so that approaching drivers can see pedestrians and traffic.

question: Turning onto a two-lane road marked by a broken yellow centerline tells you:
options: a:The road is under repair.,b:You are on a two-way road.,c:You are on a one-way road.
note: Broken yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and may be crossed to pass when it is safe.

question: Guide signs that give directions and mileage information are usually what color?
options: a:Yellow,b:Red,c:Green
note: Guide or destination signs are typically green with white lettering and provide directional and distance information.

question: When an oncoming vehicle is approaching at night, your headlights should be set to:
options: a:High-beam headlights,b:Off; use parking lights only,c:Low-beam headlights
note: Do not use high beams when another vehicle is approaching or when following another vehicle; use low beams to avoid blinding other drivers.

question: If you need to slow on a slippery road, what should you do first?
options: a:Apply the parking brake.,b:Firmly apply your brakes.,c:Take your foot off the gas pedal.
note: On slippery surfaces first ease off the accelerator; if further slowing is needed apply gentle steady brake pressure.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection you should:
options: a:Yield to vehicles approaching from the right and be prepared to stop.,b:Maintain your speed and proceed.,c:Always stop at the intersection.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, take your foot off the accelerator, cover the brake, and yield to the right as needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, what's usually best?
options: a:Turn on hazards until fully merged.,b:Accelerate on the ramp to match freeway traffic speed.,c:Proceed slowly and wait for a gap.
note: Use the on-ramp to accelerate to freeway speed so you can merge smoothly; yield to vehicles already on the freeway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A steady red traffic signal requires you to:
options: a:Stop at the stop line only.,b:Stop before any crosswalk only.,c:Stop before entering the intersection.
note: A red light requires stopping before entering the intersection. If there is a stop line or crosswalk, stop before those markings; otherwise stop at a point where you can see traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who goes first?
options: a:The vehicle approaching from the left.,b:The vehicle whose driver honks first.,c:The vehicle approaching from the right.
note: At an intersection with no signs or signals, yield to the vehicle approaching from the right.

question: Warning signs indicating upcoming hazards usually have what colors?
options: a:Black letters or symbols on a white background.,b:White letters or symbols on a blue background.,c:Black letters or symbols on a yellow background.
note: Hazard warning signs are typically yellow with black lettering; work zone warnings are orange with black symbols.

question: If you leave your vehicle unattended you must:
options: a:Set the parking brake only.,b:Lock the ignition and remove the key.,c:Turn off the engine only.
note: When leaving a vehicle unattended you must stop the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

question: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in which situations?
options: a:Only when the pedestrian is on the same side of the road.,b:Always,c:Only in marked crosswalks.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the street even if they are acting carelessly or crossing against a signal.

question: When is a right turn on red prohibited?
options: a:Only when a pedestrian is present.,b:When a walk signal is showing for a crosswalk or a sign prohibits right on red.,c:When a vehicle is in the intersection on the opposite side.
note: Right turns on red are prohibited where a sign forbids them or when a walk signal is displayed for a crosswalk, even if no pedestrians are visible.

question: If you're involved in a collision, what should you do first?
options: a:Drive away if the damage is minor.,b:Stop immediately and assist the injured as needed.,c:Call your insurance company and then leave.
note: Stop immediately, move vehicles out of traffic if possible, call the police and emergency services if needed, and assist injured persons without moving them unnecessarily.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a Merging traffic sign on the freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Make room for entering vehicles by changing lanes if possible.,b:Always remain at your present speed.,c:Honk at incoming traffic to warn them.
note: On multi-lane roads, adjust speed or change lanes when safe to allow merging traffic to enter.

question: If you must drive in fog, use which headlights?
options: a:Parking lights,b:High-beam headlights,c:Low-beam headlights
note: High beams reflect off fog and reduce visibility; use low beams (and fog lights if available) to see better in fog.

question: A pennant-shaped traffic sign is used to indicate:
options: a:A speed limit.,b:A no passing zone.,c:A school zone.
note: Pennant-shaped signs are used to warn drivers they are entering a no passing zone; text on the sign confirms the restriction.

question: When driving near a motorcycle you must:
options: a:Allow the motorcycle to use only half a lane.,b:Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.,c:Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.
note: A motorcycle is a full-size vehicle entitled to the use of an entire lane; give it space to maneuver.

question: What must you do with your headlights when driving in rain?
options: a:Use parking lights only.,b:Use low beam headlights.,c:Use high beam headlights.
note: In rainy conditions use low beam headlights so you can see and be seen without causing excessive glare.

question: If your vehicle's turn signals are not working, how should you show other road users your intentions?
options: a:Use hand signals to indicate turns and lane changes.,b:Use your headlights.,c:Sound your horn instead.
note: When turn signals fail, use hand signals to show other drivers when you intend to turn or change lanes.

question: What is the purpose of an advisory speed sign attached to a curve warning sign?
options: a:To indicate a minimum legal speed.,b:To be ignored in rain or snow.,c:To recommend a safe speed for the curve which should be reduced in poor conditions.
note: Advisory speeds suggest a safe speed for curves under normal conditions; reduce speed further when weather or road conditions are poor.

question: If you are stopped by a police officer, you should:
options: a:Get your paperwork ready and then exit the vehicle to meet the officer.,b:Stay in your vehicle with your hands visible on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach.,c:Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window before the officer reaches you.
note: Remain in the vehicle with hands visible and wait for the officer to request your license and registration; only exit if asked to do so.

question: Which of these suggestions is least directly related to promoting safe night driving?
options: a:Carry a small flashlight in your vehicle.,b:Be aware that tinted windows reduce visibility at night.,c:Keep your windshield clean.
note: While a flashlight can be useful in emergencies, safe night driving primarily depends on clear windows, proper lighting, and avoiding reduced visibility from tinted glass.

question: When you see a blind pedestrian who is using a white cane or guide dog, you should:
options: a:Take the right-of-way,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop,c:Proceed normally without reducing speed.
note: When encountering a blind pedestrian using a cane or guide dog, you must yield and be prepared to stop to avoid harm.

question: On average, how many alcoholic drinks does the body eliminate in one hour?
options: a:About one drink per hour.,b:About three drinks per hour.,c:About two drinks per hour.
note: An average person's body metabolizes about one standard drink per hour, though many factors affect impairment.

question: What is the No zone in relation to large trucks or buses?
options: a:A restricted audio volume area for vehicle stereos.,b:The blind spots around a truck or bus where the driver cannot see you.,c:A special speed zone around large vehicles.
note: Large vehicles have blind spots on each side, in front, and behind; these are called No zones.

question: What happens when you take drugs along with alcohol?
options: a:The combined use increases the risk of causing a crash.,b:The combination is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.,c:The drugs lessen alcohol's effect on driving.
note: Combining alcohol with drugs (prescription, over-the-counter, or illegal) increases impairment and crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp you should generally do what?
options: a:Enter slowly to avoid other vehicles.,b:Stop on the ramp then enter.,c:Use the acceleration lane to reach highway speed and merge with traffic.
note: Use acceleration lanes to accelerate to the speed of traffic and merge when you find a safe gap; yield to vehicles already on the highway.

question: If a transit vehicle signals to re-enter the main road after stopping, what must you do?
options: a:Honking to alert the driver.,b:Maintain speed and position.,c:Yield and allow it to safely re-enter.
note: Yield to transit vehicles signaling to re-enter traffic after stopping to load or unload passengers; change lanes or slow to allow them to merge safely.

question: What effect does even a small amount of alcohol have on driving-related abilities?
options: a:Only a blood alcohol level greater than the legal limit will reduce these abilities.,b:Even the smallest amount of alcohol can reduce concentration,c:Alcohol does not reduce these driving abilities.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol impair concentration, perception, judgment, and memory; no one can safely drink and drive.

question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?
options: a:Never if there are no trains visible.,b:Only if flashing red signals are present.,c:When directed by a flagger or stop sign.
note: Stop at railroad crossings when directed by a flagger or stop sign; also stop when flashing red signals or lowered gates indicate a train is coming.

question: When making a turn, you must do what to your speed?
options: a:Increase your speed.,b:Maintain or vary your speed at will.,c:Reduce your speed to maintain control.
note: Reduce speed when turning to stay in your lane, maintain control, and react to unexpected hazards.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid you should:
options: a:Overcorrect the steering.,b:Turn the steering wheel in the direction of the skid.,c:Turn the steering wheel into oncoming traffic.
note: If your vehicle skids, remain calm and steer in the direction of the skid to regain control.

question: What should you do to avoid collisions with vehicles in your blind spots?
options: a:Honk your horn right before changing lanes.,b:Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.,c:Turn your head and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots before changing lanes.
note: Never rely solely on mirrors; check blind spots by looking over your shoulder before lane changes.

question: Compared to daytime driving, how is night driving different?
options: a:Less dangerous.,b:The same as daytime driving.,c:More dangerous because visibility is reduced.
note: Night driving is more hazardous due to reduced visibility, glare from lights, and more fatigued or impaired drivers on the road.

question: On long trips you can prevent drowsiness by:
options: a:Stopping at regular intervals for rest.,b:Turning on the car radio.,c:Slowing down.
note: Take regular breaks to rest and stretch during long trips to avoid drowsiness.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are moving from the right lane into the left lane on a multilane highway, what checks should you make?
options: a:Look in mirrors and over your left shoulder for traffic in the blind spot,b:Only look in the rearview mirror and then change lanes quickly.,c:Signal and assume the lane is clear without looking.
note: Before changing lanes, check mirrors, glance over your shoulder to cover blind spots, and signal your intention.

question: Which of the following substances can impair driving and lead to DUII charges?
options: a:Only alcohol.,b:Beer,c:Only illegal drugs.
note: Many substances—including alcoholic beverages, illegal drugs, inhalants, and some medicines—can impair driving and lead to arrest.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On most roadways you should signal your intent to turn at least:
options: a:300 feet before the turn.,b:500 feet before the turn.,c:100 feet before the turn.
note: Signal at least 100 feet before a turn on most roads; on highways signal farther in advance.

question: If you are in an accident and someone is injured, what should you do?
options: a:Do not move the injured unless necessary; keep them warm and provide first aid if able.,b:Move the injured immediately away from the scene.,c:Always leave injured people where they are without attempting aid.
note: Avoid moving injured persons unless required, keep them warm, and apply first aid for severe bleeding until help arrives.

question: If you start to feel tired while driving, what is the best action?
options: a:Stop driving and rest.,b:Have some coffee and keep driving.,c:Open the window and continue.
note: Fatigue is dangerous and comparable to impaired driving; stop and rest rather than continuing to drive.

question: To reduce headlight glare from oncoming vehicles at night, where should you look?
options: a:Over your shoulder.,b:Straight at the oncoming headlights.,c:Toward the right side of the road ahead.
note: If oncoming drivers don't dim high beams, keep your eyes on the right side of the road to avoid being blinded.

question: Lack of sleep affects driving ability similar to which of these?
options: a:The effects of amphetamines.,b:The effects of anger.,c:The effects of alcohol on driving performance.
note: Fatigue impairs driving much like alcohol; e.g., being awake 18 hours has impairment similar to BAC 0.05% and 24 hours like 0.10%.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Brake hard when entering standing water.,b:Drive more quickly through shallow water.,c:Drive more slowly in wet conditions.
note: Hydroplaning risk increases with speed; slowing down in wet conditions reduces that risk.

question: Which practice best helps ensure safety when backing your vehicle?
options: a:Honk just before shifting into reverse.,b:Check only the rearview mirrors.,c:Walk to the rear of the vehicle and check behind it before getting in.
note: Backing is hazardous because drivers have limited rear visibility. Before entering the vehicle to back up, walk around to check for children or objects.

question: Under normal conditions, what is the minimum following distance you should keep?
options: a:Three seconds.,b:One second.,c:Two seconds.
note: Keep at least a three-second following distance under normal conditions; increase this distance when conditions worsen.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic signal requires you to:
options: a:Stop and then proceed when it is safe (same as a stop sign).,b:Slow down and yield,c:Slow down but do not stop.
note: A flashing red light means stop completely and then proceed only when the way is clear, just like a stop sign.

question: You may not legally park your vehicle in which of the following locations?
options: a:On a hill.,b:In a parking lot.,c:On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
note: Parking is prohibited in crosswalks and marked bicycle lanes, among other restricted areas; when parking on the street you must be within 12 inches of the curb.

question: If you have a green light but pedestrians are crossing against the light, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to pass in front of them.,b:Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.,c:Honk to make them hurry.
note: You must yield to pedestrians even if they are crossing against a signal; stop to allow them to cross safely.

question: When roads may be slippery you should:
options: a:Use cruise control to maintain speed.,b:Reduce your following distance.,c:Always drive at the maximum speed limit.
note: On slippery surfaces reduce speed, avoid sudden changes, and do not use cruise control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road, you must:
options: a:Use the shoulder.,b:Not cross the centerline.,c:Use the lane belonging to oncoming traffic to complete the pass.
note: Passing on a two-lane, two-way road usually requires entering the lane of oncoming traffic to complete the pass; do so only when it is safe and legal.

question: How should you regard railroad crossings?
options: a:Safe to cross in most cases.,b:Always potentially dangerous.,c:A safe place to park.
note: Railroad crossings are always potentially dangerous; always look and listen for approaching trains and obey signals.

question: Drivers who eat or drink while driving:
options: a:Are better drivers because they are not hungry.,b:Are more likely to have trouble staying in their lane and controlling the vehicle.,c:Make no driving errors.
note: Eating or drinking while driving distracts you and can cause lane and speed control problems.

question: When approaching railroad tracks you should:
options: a:Try to drive around a lowered gate.,b:Look,c:Speed up to cross before gates lower.
note: Always look and listen for trains, slow down, and be prepared to stop at railroad crossings.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If driving on a one-way street and an emergency vehicle using lights approaches, what must you do?
options: a:Speed up and exit the roadway.,b:Turn on your hazard flashers and keep going.,c:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.
note: On a one-way street you must drive to the nearest roadside and stop for an emergency vehicle using lights or siren.

question: In poor weather conditions, what should drivers do regarding following distance?
options: a:Decrease their following distance.,b:Maintain the same following distance as in dry conditions.,c:Increase their following distance.
note: On wet, icy, or otherwise poor roads, increase the distance between vehicles to allow more stopping time.

question: Under which circumstance may you drive around lowered gates at a railroad crossing?
options: a:When the lights stop flashing.,b:When the train has passed.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: Do not go around lowered crossing gates. You must stop when signals warn of an approaching train and wait until it is safe and legal to proceed.

question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?
options: a:No passing is permitted in either direction.,b:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid line.,c:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken line.
note: A broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line allows passing for vehicles on the broken-line side when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you pass another vehicle by using the right shoulder?
options: a:When the car in front is driving too slowly.,b:Never.,c:When the car in front is turning.
note: You may not drive off the pavement or onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle; passing on the shoulder is prohibited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection and opposing traffic blocks your view, what should you do?
options: a:Accelerate rapidly when the first lane clears.,b:Signal and rely on another driver to wave you through.,c:Wait until you can see all lanes you must cross before making the turn.
note: Do not begin a left turn until you can see that all lanes are clear and you can make the turn safely.

question: When driving near heavy trucks, what should other road users allow for?
options: a:The lower noise levels of large vehicles.,b:The decreased stopping distance of large vehicles.,c:The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.
note: Trucks need more distance to stop; avoid lingering in their blind spots and position your vehicle where you are visible to the truck driver.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where should you NOT pass other vehicles?
options: a:On an expressway only.,b:Whenever the lane looks clear.,c:On a hill or curve.
note: Never pass on a hill or curve, near intersections, railroad crossings, bridges, or where your view is blocked or where signs prohibit passing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching a steady yellow traffic light you should:
options: a:Continue because you have the right-of-way.,b:Accelerate to avoid a red light.,c:Slow to a stop unless you are already in the intersection.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the light will turn red; stop unless it is unsafe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a steady green arrow at a signal, what may drivers do?
options: a:Stop before proceeding in the arrow's direction.,b:Merge into any lane regardless of direction.,c:Turn in the direction of the arrow after yielding to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.
note: A steady green arrow allows turning in the arrow's direction after yielding to others in the intersection.

question: If your vehicle’s right wheels leave the pavement, what is the recommended action?
options: a:Slow down,b:Accelerate and steer back onto the road as fast as possible.,c:Stop quickly immediately.
note: Do not panic. Gradually reduce speed, keep the vehicle straight, and ease back onto the roadway when it is safe while checking for traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When the driver behind you wants to pass, what is the correct action?
options: a:Slow down to allow room in front of your vehicle for the pass.,b:Maintain the same speed.,c:Speed up to prevent them from passing.
note: Slow slightly to create space in front of your vehicle so the other driver can pass safely and complete the maneuver quickly.

question: When it starts to rain while you're driving, what is the correct action?
options: a:Slow down.,b:Maintain the maximum posted speed limit.,c:Drive faster than surrounding traffic.
note: When rain begins reduce speed, turn on headlights for visibility, and pull off if conditions become too severe to continue safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When exiting a highway, when should you begin to slow down?
options: a:Once you see a toll booth.,b:After you have moved into the exit lane.,c:On the main road just before the exit lane.
note: Move into the exit lane well in advance and do not slow down until you are in that exit lane.

question: A steady yellow traffic light approaching an intersection tells you to:
options: a:Go.,b:Yield to other cars.,c:Slow down and prepare to stop.
note: A steady yellow light warns that a red light will soon follow. Slow down and prepare to stop unless you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which traffic light condition is equivalent to coming to a full stop, yielding, then proceeding when clear?
options: a:A flashing yellow light.,b:A solid green light.,c:A flashing red light.
note: A flashing red traffic light requires you to stop completely, yield to cross traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when safe—like a stop sign.

question: If an approaching vehicle is using high beams and fails to dim them, you should look toward:
options: a:Either side of the road.,b:The center of the road.,c:The right side of the road.
note: Glance toward the right edge of the road to avoid being blinded by high beams while maintaining your lane position.

question: The most effective safety restraints in a crash are:
options: a:Only a lap and shoulder belt.,b:Only an airbag.,c:Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
note: Seat belts and airbags together provide the best protection in a front-end crash; always use both.

question: Why must you use extra caution around a pedestrian carrying a white cane?
options: a:They are police officers directing traffic.,b:They are deaf and cannot hear your horn.,c:They are likely blind and require yielding and extra caution.
note: A white cane or guide dog indicates blindness — slow down, yield, and be prepared to stop.

question: Regulatory traffic signs are usually which color?
options: a:Green,b:White,c:Blue
note: Regulatory signs (such as speed limit and stop signs) are typically white with black letters and must be obeyed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first after signaling and checking traffic?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the right immediately.,b:Turn your wheels to the left immediately.,c:Pull up even with the car in front of the space
note: Stop parallel to the vehicle ahead of the space before turning the wheel to back into the spot.

question: When dealing with pedestrians, what is the driver's obligation?
options: a:Only yield if the pedestrian is legally entitled to it.,b:Make sure the pedestrian is aware of the vehicle before yielding.,c:Yield the right-of-way to all pedestrians and do everything possible to avoid striking them.
note: Drivers must be alert and yield to pedestrians to prevent injury, even if pedestrians are crossing illegally.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers may not pass from either side of a ____ centerline.
options: a:Single broken yellow,b:Combination solid and broken yellow,c:Double solid yellow
note: A double solid yellow centerline means passing from either direction is prohibited.

question: You may pass another vehicle if the line dividing the lanes is what type of line?
options: a:Double solid yellow line.,b:Solid yellow line.,c:Broken white line.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to pass when safe.

question: When driving where children are playing, what should you expect?
options: a:They will always stop at the curb before crossing.,b:They will know when it's safe to cross.,c:They may run into the street without looking.
note: Expect children to behave unpredictably and possibly run into the roadway without checking for traffic; slow down and be alert.

question: If someone is driving aggressively behind you, you should:
options: a:Speed up as they pass you.,b:Stare at the driver as they pass.,c:Attempt to get out of their way.
note: Move out of the aggressive driver's path, avoid eye contact, and do not escalate the situation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless posted otherwise, the speed limit in an urban residence district is:
options: a:40 miles per hour.,b:30 miles per hour.,c:55 miles per hour.
note: In an urban residence district the speed limit is normally 30 mph unless otherwise posted.

question: On a highway marked by two solid yellow centerlines, you may:
options: a:Cross these lines only to make a left turn into or from an alley,b:Never cross these lines under any circumstances.,c:Cross these lines to pass if no oncoming traffic is present.
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing; you may only cross them to make a left turn into or from a private road, alley, or driveway.

question: Which factors commonly cause traffic accidents?
options: a:Inattentive driving,b:Only vehicle defects.,c:Safe driving habits of other motorists.
note: Major causes of crashes include inattention, driving too fast for conditions, and following other vehicles too closely.

question: When are roads especially slippery due to rain?
options: a:During the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.,b:The day after it rains.,c:Only after it has been raining for an hour.
note: Road surfaces can be especially slippery in the first 10–15 minutes of rain because oil and residue rise to the pavement surface.

question: What describes an inattentive driver?
options: a:Someone who only watches the vehicle directly ahead.,b:Someone who maintains eye contact while talking to a passenger.,c:Someone who daydreams or stares at objects off the roadway while driving.
note: An inattentive driver is distracted by things off the road, daydreaming, or otherwise not scanning the driving environment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a green arrow shown with a red light authorize you to do?
options: a:Turn only in the direction of the green arrow, if the intersection is clear.,b:Go straight ahead only.,c:Wait for a solid green circular light before moving in any direction.
note: A green arrow with a red light allows movement only in the arrow's direction, after yielding to any traffic and pedestrians in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you come to an intersection with a flashing yellow light, you should:
options: a:Stop and wait for the light to change.,b:Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.,c:Drive carefully through the intersection after yielding to any conflicting traffic.
note: A flashing yellow means proceed with caution; scan for cross traffic and pedestrians before continuing.

question: It is important to slow down in which situations?
options: a:Never — keep to the speed limit.,b:On narrow or winding roads.,c:Only when the road is wet.
note: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, at intersections, near railroad crossings, and when roads are slippery.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, the maximum speed in a rural residence district is:
options: a:45 miles per hour.,b:25 miles per hour.,c:35 miles per hour.
note: In rural residence districts the speed limit is typically 35 mph unless a different limit is posted.

question: Who should wear seat belts for maximum effectiveness?
options: a:The driver only.,b:Only passengers on long trips.,c:All occupants of the vehicle.
note: Seat belts are most effective when every occupant in the vehicle wears one on every trip.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit indicate?
options: a:The exact safe speed you must always drive to avoid a ticket.,b:Only a recommended driving speed.,c:The maximum legal driving speed under ideal road and weather conditions.
note: Speed limit signs show the maximum legal speed for ideal conditions; drivers must drive slower when conditions require.

question: If a crossing guard directs traffic in a school zone, you must do what?
options: a:Copy surrounding traffic even if it contradicts the guard.,b:Follow the crossing guard's directions.,c:Assume they are not authorized to direct traffic.
note: Always obey the directions of a crossing guard in a school zone and be prepared to reduce speed and use caution.

question: What does a yellow-and-black diamond-shaped sign indicate?
options: a:Traffic laws and regulations you must obey.,b:A warning about conditions on or near the road ahead.,c:Directions to nearby cities and towns.
note: Diamond-shaped yellow warning signs alert drivers to upcoming road conditions or hazards.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing with warning signs, what should you be prepared to do?
options: a:Proceed without slowing unless you see a train.,b:Cross quickly if a train is approaching.,c:Slow down
note: On approach to a railroad crossing slow down, look both ways, and be ready to stop. If signals or gates are active, stop at the indicated distance from the tracks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How close to a bridge, viaduct, or tunnel is passing prohibited?
options: a:Within 100 feet.,b:Within 300 feet.,c:Within 200 feet.
note: Passing is not allowed within 100 feet of a bridge, viaduct, or tunnel so other drivers can see you attempting to pass.

question: For persons age 21 and older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of at least:
options: a:0.02 percent,b:0.08 percent,c:0.05 percent
note: For drivers 21 and older, a BAC of 0.08% or higher is illegal and indicates impairment for driving.

question: A red and white triangular sign at an intersection means you must:
options: a:Speed up if an emergency vehicle is approaching.,b:Always come to a full stop.,c:Yield — slow and be prepared to stop if necessary.
note: A triangular yield sign means you must decrease speed and yield the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians.

question: How can stress affect your driving?
options: a:By decreasing your chance of an accident.,b:By causing you to fall asleep at the wheel.,c:By reducing your ability to focus and concentrate on driving.
note: Strong emotions and stress can impair concentration and driving performance; wait to drive if you're emotionally unstable.

question: When approaching an accident scene you should:
options: a:Always stop and watch.,b:Drive toward the scene to see what happened.,c:Stop only if you are involved or emergency help has not yet arrived.
note: Do not stop at an accident unless you are involved or emergency assistance is needed and has not yet arrived.

question: When is it legal to stop or park along the shoulder of a freeway?
options: a:If no part of your vehicle is on the roadway.,b:Only in an emergency.,c:As long as you turn on your four-way flashers.
note: Parking on the shoulder of a freeway is prohibited except in an emergency; if you must stop, turn on hazard lights and move as far from traffic as possible.

question: A diamond-shaped traffic sign is normally used to:
options: a:Indicate a school crossing.,b:Indicate an interstate route.,c:Warn of a road hazard or special condition.
note: Warning signs are typically diamond-shaped and warn of hazardous locations or where special rules apply.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must yield when a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light?
options: a:Whoever is slower.,b:Whoever started moving last.,c:The driver must yield to the pedestrian.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at intersections without traffic signals, even if there is no marked crosswalk.

question: What is likely to happen when alcohol is combined with another drug?
options: a:The effects of both may be reduced.,b:Nothing will happen.,c:The effects of both the alcohol and the drug may be increased.
note: Mixing alcohol with another drug can enhance the effects of both, increasing impairment and danger.

question: Which statement about winter driving is NOT true?
options: a:Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.,b:Checking antifreeze and washer fluid is especially important in winter.,c:Winter is the most difficult driving season.
note: Using cruise control in snow, ice, or similar hazardous conditions is unsafe; winter requires extra caution and vehicle checks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto an interstate from an entrance ramp, you should:
options: a:Have the right-of-way over traffic on the interstate.,b:Force your way into traffic if necessary.,c:Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
note: Vehicles already on the interstate have the right-of-way. Use the acceleration lane to match speed and merge safely when there is a gap.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a multilane highway you should:
options: a:Watch for oncoming traffic in the opposite direction.,b:Always pass only on the right.,c:Be sure the passing lane is clear before changing lanes.
note: Make sure the lane you plan to enter is clear and signal before changing lanes to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left, what should drivers do?
options: a:Signal only if other traffic is present.,b:Slow down gradually without checking mirrors.,c:Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians and yield when necessary.
note: Signal 3–5 seconds before turning, check mirrors and blind spots, yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic, and complete the turn when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you encounter a flashing red light at an intersection, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and drive carefully through.,b:Wait for a flashing green light.,c:Come to a complete stop and proceed only when the way is clear.
note: A flashing red light means stop like a stop sign; yield to traffic and pedestrians before proceeding.

question: If your vehicle's accelerator sticks while driving, which action should you take?
options: a:Slam on the brakes immediately and hold them.,b:Turn on your hazard flashers,c:Blow your horn continuously until help arrives.
note: For a stuck accelerator, shift to neutral, apply brakes, move safely off the road, then turn off the engine (careful not to lock steering).

question: When sharing the road with a large truck remember trucks generally:
options: a:Require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.,b:Require less time to pass on a downgrade.,c:Require a smaller turning radius than smaller vehicles.
note: Because of their size and weight, large vehicles need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles.

question: If your car breaks down on the highway, you should:
options: a:Use your four-way flashers,b:Sound your horn to attract passing motorists' attention.,c:Sit in your car and wait for help without signaling
note: Signal and carefully exit the traffic lane, turn on hazard lights, and move well off the roadway so other drivers can see you; raise your hood if you want to indicate a disabled vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a stop sign with no stop line or crosswalk, you may proceed only:
options: a:After slowing down to check for cross traffic.,b:After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.,c:After coming to a complete stop and verifying it is safe to proceed.
note: Stop before entering the intersection and go only when it is safe to do so.

question: What colors are used on highway destination/distance signs (like exit signs)?
options: a:Black background with white letters.,b:Yellow background with black letters.,c:Green background with white letters or symbols.
note: Destination and distance signs use a green background with white letters or symbols.

question: Why is night driving often harder than daytime driving?
options: a:Because visibility is reduced in the dark.,b:Because it is more likely to rain at night.,c:Because cars overheat more easily at night.
note: At night your field of vision is reduced; use proper headlights and drive at speeds that let you stop within the visible distance.

question: When a funeral procession is present, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Any other driver.,b:A pedestrian.,c:The funeral procession.
note: Drivers, pedestrians, and bicyclists must yield the right-of-way to funeral processions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is driving below the posted speed limit illegal?
options: a:Only while driving in rural areas.,b:When in heavy traffic in a construction zone.,c:When driving so slowly that you disrupt the normal flow of traffic.
note: It's illegal to drive so slowly that you impede normal traffic flow; you may be required to pull over and let vehicles pass.

question: What road markings or signals direct drivers into proper turning lanes on some highways?
options: a:Flashing red lights.,b:Arrows painted or displayed to indicate lane purposes.,c:White lines on the side of the road only.
note: Arrows (pavement markings or signal displays) indicate which lanes should be used for turning or going straight.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A posted speed limit represents what?
options: a:The maximum or minimum legal speed under ideal conditions.,b:The legal speed under dangerous conditions.,c:A suggested safe speed for the area.
note: A speed limit is the legal maximum or minimum under ideal conditions; you must drive slower when conditions require it.

question: What should a driver do if going much slower than the speed limit and causing a backup?
options: a:Pull off the road and allow vehicles to pass.,b:Refuse to let following cars pass.,c:Continue; slower speeds are always safer.
note: If you drive significantly slower than the flow of traffic and vehicles are backing up, you must pull off and let others pass if possible.

question: On slippery roads you should do which of the following?
options: a:Drive as you would on dry roads.,b:Increase your following distance.,c:Use alternate routes only.
note: Slippery conditions increase stopping distances so you should increase the space between you and the vehicle ahead.

question: If you notice other drivers behaving angrily on the road, you should:
options: a:Make eye contact to let them know you won't be intimidated.,b:React with hand gestures to show your displeasure.,c:Distance yourself from the situation (physically and mentally).
note: When other drivers show anger, avoid eye contact and gestures and take steps to put distance between you and the situation to reduce the risk of escalation.

question: If you are in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?
options: a:Stay there until you need to pass.,b:Keep a steady pace in the blind spot.,c:Move forward or fall back so the driver can see you.
note: Avoid driving in someone else's blind spot; adjust your position so the driver can see you in their mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before making a left turn you must:
options: a:Swing to the right side of your lane before turning.,b:Sound your horn to warn others.,c:Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.
note: Yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before completing a left turn; do not turn into the path of oncoming vehicles.

question: If you become stranded during a snowstorm, what should you do?
options: a:Lie down inside the car and go to sleep.,b:Wait in your vehicle for help to arrive.,c:Leave the car and walk for assistance.
note: If stranded in a snowstorm you should stay with your vehicle and wait for help; you're more likely to be found and it's often unsafe to walk in such conditions.

question: What is the safest way to drive through a curve?
options: a:Slow down as you enter the curve and accelerate gradually as you exit.,b:Keep a constant speed throughout the curve.,c:Speed up as you enter the curve and slow down as you exit.
note: Reduce speed before entering a curve and then increase speed gradually when your wheels are straight to maintain control.

question: Where should you keep a space cushion around your vehicle?
