options: a:Only in front of your vehicle.,b:Only on the left and right sides.,c:On all sides — front
note: Maintain space all around your vehicle to allow time to react to hazards.

question: When approached by an emergency vehicle using lights or siren, you must:
options: a:Pull to the right and turn on your four-way flashers.,b:Pull to the right and slow down.,c:Pull to the right side of the road and stop immediately.
note: You must yield to emergency vehicles by pulling to the right and stopping to allow them to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In a vertically arranged traffic signal, what is the correct top-to-bottom order of the lights?
options: a:Yellow,b:Green,c:Red
note: On vertical signals red is always at the top, yellow in the middle, and green on the bottom.

question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Keep the wheels straight and set the parking brake.,b:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,c:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn wheels away from the curb so the vehicle will roll back into the curb and not into traffic if the brakes fail.

question: Which factors affect braking distance?
options: a:Speed,b:Only the vehicle's weight.,c:Only the driver’s reaction time.
note: Braking distance depends on speed, brake and tire condition, and road surface condition, among other factors.

question: What driving habit helps conserve gasoline?
options: a:Accelerating quickly from stops.,b:Sitting in the driveway with the engine running.,c:Slowing down gradually and avoiding unnecessary braking.
note: Smooth driving—looking ahead and slowing gradually—reduces unnecessary acceleration and improves fuel economy.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When an emergency vehicle uses sirens or flashing lights, what must drivers do?
options: a:Stop immediately in your lane and wait for it to pass no matter where you are.,b:Ignore it if you are in a hurry.,c:Yield the right-of-way to it and follow any instructions it gives.
note: Yield to emergency vehicles using sirens or lights; obey any directions and be aware they may be followed by others.

question: On slippery roads you should:
options: a:Drive the speed limit with no extra caution.,b:Drive more quickly.,c:Slow down.
note: Reduce speed and avoid sudden maneuvers when road surfaces are slippery; consider driving below the posted limit if needed.

question: When children ride in a vehicle, they should:
options: a:Stand on the floor in the back of the vehicle.,b:Be properly fastened in an appropriate child safety seat if too small for a regular belt.,c:Be safely held by a strong adult.
note: Special child seats are required for children too small for regular safety belts; holding them is not safe in a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you signal while turning or changing lanes?
options: a:Only when driving at night.,b:Always,c:Only when other vehicles are present.
note: You must always signal when changing lanes, turning, or pulling away from a curb; do not form the habit of not signaling.

question: What effect does alcohol have on driving skills and judgment?
options: a:It has no effect on either.,b:It helps driving skills but harms judgment.,c:It harms both driving skills and judgment.
note: Alcohol impairs reaction time, vision, judgment, and increases the likelihood of risky behavior.

question: A pentagonal (five-sided) traffic sign warns drivers they are near:
options: a:A no passing zone.,b:A speed limit change.,c:A school zone or school crossing.
note: Pentagonal signs indicate school zones and school crossings. Be alert to children and comply with any speed reductions.

question: What does a solid red arrow in a traffic signal mean?
options: a:It has the same meaning as a circular red light; you must stop.,b:It is never used.,c:It means drivers may turn in the arrow direction.
note: A solid red arrow requires drivers in the indicated lane to stop and prohibits turning in that direction while red.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct procedure when using a freeway exit ramp?
options: a:Slow down before you move onto the exit ramp.,b:Maintain your freeway speed until the ramp ends.,c:Slow down once you are on the exit ramp.
note: Do not reduce speed on the mainline; instead, slow down after you have moved onto the exit ramp in the deceleration area.

question: To avoid being in a truck or bus driver's blind spot you should:
options: a:Flash your lights at them.,b:Never pass them.,c:Avoid driving alongside them and avoid tailgating.
note: Large vehicles have significant side and rear blind spots; avoid driving alongside or tailgating them.

question: A solid yellow arrow traffic signal means:
options: a:It is not used as a traffic control signal.,b:Drivers may turn in the direction indicated without caution.,c:The same as a circular yellow light — prepare to stop.
note: A solid yellow arrow warns that the protected turning time is ending; slow down and prepare to stop if it is safe to do so.

question: A road work area or work zone may be which of the following?
options: a:Moving or stationary.,b:A place where drivers do not have to slow down or pay attention.,c:Marked with black and white signs.
note: Work zones can be stationary or involve moving operations; they are typically marked with orange signs and require drivers to slow down and pay added attention.

question: How does increasing your vehicle's speed affect your field of vision?
options: a:It increases your field of vision.,b:It decreases your field of vision.,c:It makes it easier to see cross traffic.
note: As speed increases your field of vision narrows, so you must be extra alert to hazards.

question: Which types of drugs can impair driving ability?
options: a:Only illegal drugs.,b:Prescription and over-the-counter medications,c:Only alcohol-related medicines.
note: Many kinds of drugs—legal or illegal—can impair driving. Driving under the influence of drugs can be a criminal offense.

question: Foggy conditions require which of these actions?
options: a:Turn on your low-beam headlights.,b:Turn on your hazard lights only.,c:Drive at the posted maximum speed.
note: Use low-beam headlights in fog (and when visibility is reduced to 500 feet or less); high beams worsen visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A red flashing traffic light is equivalent to which traffic control device?
options: a:A stop sign.,b:A steady red light only.,c:A yield sign.
note: A flashing red signal means you must stop completely and proceed only when safe, just like a stop sign.

question: What does a “No standing” sign mean at a location?
options: a:You may stop only briefly to pick up or discharge passengers.,b:You may park there if you stay with the vehicle.,c:You may never stop there for any reason.
note: A No Standing sign allows temporary stopping only to load or unload passengers; parking is not permitted.

question: What should you do before switching on the ignition?
options: a:Confirm only adult passengers are belted.,b:Only make sure children are belted.,c:Buckle your seat belt and ensure passengers are buckled.
note: Develop a routine of buckling your safety belt and ensuring all passengers are buckled before starting the vehicle.

question: If you face an oncoming car on your left and a bicyclist on your right, what should you do?
options: a:Pull onto the shoulder to pass between both.,b:Split the difference and move between them.,c:Let the oncoming car pass first
note: When multiple hazards exist, handle one at a time: allow the oncoming vehicle to pass, then pass the bicyclist safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it appropriate to sound your horn?
options: a:Whenever you have to stop quickly.,b:When passing another car.,c:If you have lost control of your vehicle and need to alert others.
note: Use your horn to warn others of immediate danger—e.g., if you have lost control and need to alert drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are required to stop your vehicle:
options: a:Only when a police officer orders you to.,b:At an intersection with a stop sign.,c:Only where there is a flashing yellow light.
note: You must stop at stop signs, at red lights, and whenever a traffic officer orders you to stop.

question: When must you stop for a school bus on a two-lane highway?
options: a:Only when the bus is facing you and its lights are flashing.,b:Only if the bus is parked on the shoulder with no one aboard.,c:When the bus is stopped and its red lights are flashing.
note: On two-lane roads, traffic in both directions must stop when a school bus displays flashing red lights while loading or unloading children.

question: Highway pavement markings generally:
options: a:Provide information and guidance for drivers.,b:Are usually not important.,c:Are only found in construction zones.
note: Markings help drivers position their vehicles, show safe passing zones, and warn of upcoming conditions.

question: To make night driving safer you should:
options: a:Increase your following distance to give more stopping time.,b:Always use your high beams.,c:Drive at the same following distance as daytime
note: At night, visibility is reduced; increase following distance, avoid driving tired, and make sure your headlights are in good condition.

question: How do blind spots of larger vehicles compare to those of smaller cars?
options: a:Larger vehicles have smaller blind spots.,b:Larger vehicles have larger blind spots.,c:Larger vehicles have no blind spots.
note: The larger the vehicle, such as trucks and SUVs, the larger the blind spots around it; avoid lingering in these areas.

question: If you are worried, nervous, angry, or crying before driving you should:
options: a:Drive faster because you are more alert.,b:Drive no differently than usual.,c:Take time to calm down and focus on driving before starting the engine.
note: Emotional distress can impair driving ability; take time to calm down before driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you not cross a single broken white or yellow line?
options: a:When the car in front is disabled.,b:When turning left into a driveway.,c:When doing so would interfere with traffic.
note: You may cross a single broken line to change lanes or pass only when it can be done safely without interfering with traffic.

question: Two solid white lines across a lane indicate a crosswalk. What must drivers do when pedestrians are in a crosswalk?
options: a:Proceed because no one has right-of-way there.,b:Give pedestrians the right-of-way and stop for them.,c:Assert that motor vehicles have the right-of-way.
note: Crosswalk markings show where pedestrians should cross; drivers must stop for pedestrians who are in the crosswalk.

question: If you drink alcohol socially, which action helps ensure safe driving?
options: a:Drink coffee before driving.,b:Take a cold shower before driving.,c:Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
note: Arranging a sober ride home prevents driving while impaired; coffee or a cold shower do not lower blood alcohol.

question: What is the primary purpose of regulatory signs?
options: a:To indicate what drivers must or must not do.,b:To be diamond-shaped and yellow or green.,c:To mark every location with present danger.
note: Regulatory signs tell drivers about laws and regulations (e.g., speed limits, no-turn zones) that must be followed.

question: What should car drivers remember about large trucks?
options: a:They can stop more quickly than cars.,b:They have large blind spots and need more room to maneuver and stop.,c:They need less room to turn than passenger vehicles.
note: Large trucks have significant blind spots and require more distance and space to maneuver and stop than passenger vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a stop sign you should stop and then look in which order?
options: a:Check your rearview mirror first.,b:Move when the vehicle ahead moves.,c:Right
note: After stopping at a stop sign look right, then left, then right again to check for traffic or pedestrians before proceeding.

question: When stopped on an uphill slope, when should you allow a larger space cushion?
options: a:At a stop sign only.,b:When stopped on an incline.,c:When stopped at an intersection only.
note: Allow extra space when stopped on an uphill slope since the vehicle in front might roll back when traffic begins moving again.

question: A bicyclist who disobeys traffic laws:
options: a:Will always receive a warning from law enforcement.,b:Can be ticketed.,c:Is in the right because bicyclists don’t have to obey traffic laws.
note: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicle drivers and can be ticketed for violations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a stop is required at an intersection but there are no stop lines or crosswalk markings, you should:
options: a:Not be required to stop.,b:Stop only at a point where you can see 200 feet in both directions,c:Slow down and stop at the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you have a clear view of oncoming traffic.
note: If there is no marked stop line or crosswalk, stop at the nearest point where you can see approaching traffic without entering the intersecting roadway.

question: When preparing to change lanes, which action is crucial?
options: a:Signal your intentions ahead of the lane change.,b:Make sure the lane is clear before entering.,c:Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
note: Before changing lanes always check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder so you don't rely only on mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an officer is directing traffic at an intersection, you should:
options: a:Honk at the officer to get their attention.,b:Follow the directions given by the officer.,c:Follow the traffic signal instead of the officer.
note: Drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists must obey an officer directing traffic even if traffic signals are present.

question: An arrow painted on the pavement indicates that drivers in that lane:
options: a:Must make the movement indicated by the arrow.,b:Must always stop before making the movement.,c:May make the movement if they choose.
note: A pavement arrow designates required lane movement; follow signs and signals before proceeding in that direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a highway you should signal before a turn at least:
options: a:500 feet.,b:100 feet.,c:300 feet.
note: On highways you should signal at least 500 feet before a turn to alert other drivers.

question: As alcohol accumulates in your bloodstream it typically:
options: a:Causes alcohol to metabolize more quickly.,b:Makes you feel less confident.,c:Slows down your reactions.
note: Alcohol slows reactions, increases confidence incorrectly, and causes more errors; it does not speed up its own metabolism.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic signal turns green, you should:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic already in the intersection.,b:Back up slowly if the way is blocked.,c:Accelerate as quickly as possible to clear the intersection.
note: A green light allows you to proceed, but you must first yield to pedestrians and any vehicles still in the intersection.

question: How should you safely pass a bicycle?
options: a:Slow down and give as much space as possible when passing.,b:Honk to alert them and pass quickly.,c:Drive in the bicycle lane until you can pass the rider.
note: Pass bicyclists slowly, allowing adequate space (at least 3 feet where possible) and avoid startling them.

question: Which of the following can impair a person's driving ability?
options: a:Alcohol.,b:Any medication.,c:A lack of sleep.
note: Driving ability can be impaired by alcohol, legal and illegal drugs, medications, and drowsiness.

question: What causes 'highway hypnosis'?
options: a:Too much sleep the night before your trip.,b:Staring straight ahead at the roadway for long periods of time.,c:Frequent rest stops
note: Remaining focused on the roadway center without scanning can lead to a trance-like state that reduces alertness and reaction to hazards.

question: What is the correct method to check your blind spots?
options: a:Look only in your side mirrors.,b:Turn your head and look over your shoulder.,c:Check only the rearview mirror.
note: Blind spots cannot be fully seen in mirrors; you must turn your head and glance over your shoulder to verify the area is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles enter an intersection from different highways at the same time, which vehicle must yield?
options: a:Either vehicle may proceed first.,b:The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.,c:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway you should do what?
options: a:Check rearview and side mirrors and glance over your shoulder.,b:Sound your horn.,c:Turn on your headlights.
note: Look in mirrors and check your blind spot by glancing over your shoulder before changing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a green arrow on a traffic signal mean for the lane it controls?
options: a:A green arrow is used only on one-way streets.,b:Traffic in that lane may turn in the arrow's direction; it has the same general meaning as a circular green but requires turning.,c:You may proceed only if a circular green light is also lit.
note: A green arrow permits movement in its direction; traffic in that lane must turn as indicated.

question: If you see an animal on the roadway, what is the recommended action?
options: a:Pass as closely as possible to minimize delay.,b:Honk repeatedly to move it quickly.,c:Pass the animal slowly and cautiously to avoid startling it.
note: Encounter animals with caution; slow down and pass at a safe distance to avoid causing the animal to panic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended upward, what is the driver's intended action?
options: a:The driver intends to turn left.,b:The driver intends to turn right.,c:The driver intends to stop.
note: A left arm extended upward is the hand signal for a right turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your interstate exit, what should you do?
options: a:Make a U-turn to return to the exit.,b:Continue to the next exit and do not attempt a dangerous turnback.,c:Quickly cut across traffic to make the exit.
note: If you pass your exit, continue to the next one; do not make last-minute lane changes, U-turns, or other hazardous maneuvers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A school zone speed limit is how much different than the usual posted limit?
options: a:10 miles per hour below the posted speed.,b:20 miles per hour below the posted speed.,c:10 miles per hour above the posted speed.
note: School zone limits are typically 10 mph less than the normal posted speed during specified times around the school day.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on a freeway you should:
options: a:Stop and back up to the exit.,b:Make the turn quickly from your current lane of travel.,c:Continue to the next exit or suitable turnaround and do not back up.
note: Do not stop or back up on a freeway; go to the next exit where you can safely turn around.

question: On a two-lane road without a bicycle lane, what is the safest method to pass a bicyclist?
options: a:Drive in the bike lane until you can pass quickly.,b:Force the bicyclist to move by honking.,c:Slow down
note: Pass bicyclists as you would other vehicles but allow plenty of space, at least 3 feet where possible.

question: Why should you be cautious when passing a bicycle?
options: a:Because bicycles travel much faster than cars.,b:The bicycle always has the right-of-way.,c:Oncoming traffic may not see you and the bicyclist may swerve to avoid hazards.
note: Bicyclists are smaller and may swerve unexpectedly; ensure enough clearance and watch for oncoming traffic when passing.

question: When is hand-over-hand steering recommended?
options: a:For normal cruising activity on highways.,b:When anti-lock brakes are engaged.,c:When making low-speed turns such as at intersections or parking.
note: Use hand-over-hand steering for low-speed turning maneuvers (e.g., parking or tight turns) to maintain control.

question: You should look over your shoulder to check your blind spot when you are:
options: a:Turning left or right.,b:Pulling toward or away from a curb.,c:Changing lanes.
note: Always check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder when changing lanes; also check it when turning or pulling from a curb.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights is approaching, what should you do?
options: a:Continue driving but try to stay out of its way.,b:Pull to the side of the road and stop completely when safe to do so.,c:See if you can reach your destination before it catches up.
note: Yield right-of-way to emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights; if possible, pull to the right and stop. If in an intersection, clear it then pull over.

question: Turning your head to check a blind spot before changing lanes is:
options: a:A bad driving habit.,b:A good driving habit.,c:Unnecessary.
note: Checking blind spots by looking over your shoulder is essential when changing lanes or merging; do not rely solely on mirrors.

question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle, what is the correct action?
options: a:Stop immediately where you are.,b:Proceed slowly and let it pass.,c:Drive as far right as safely possible and stop.
note: On two-lane or undivided roads you must pull as far right as is safe and stop to yield to emergency vehicles using lights or sirens.

question: Which factor does NOT affect stopping distance?
options: a:Your reaction time.,b:The time of day.,c:The condition of your brakes.
note: Stopping distance depends on reaction time, vehicle weight, brake condition, tire condition, road surface, and speed; time of day does not directly affect stopping distance.

question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off in traffic, what is the safest response?
options: a:Flash your headlights to show them they are wrong.,b:Call the police immediately.,c:Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.
note: Remain calm and get out of the aggressive driver's way; do not engage or escalate the situation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive at an open intersection simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the left.,b:The driver going straight.,c:The driver on the right.
note: At an open intersection with simultaneous arrival, yield to the vehicle on your right.

question: Does drinking coffee after drinking alcohol reduce your blood alcohol concentration?
options: a:Yes — it decreases your BAC.,b:No — it has no effect on your BAC.,c:Yes — it cancels the alcohol
note: Coffee will not lower BAC; it may make you more alert but does not change how much alcohol is in your body.

question: When should drivers use hand-to-hand (push/pull) steering?
options: a:When turning the steering wheel during normal driving activities.,b:Only when anti-lock brakes are engaged.,c:Only for low-speed turns.
note: Hand-to-hand (push/pull) steering is recommended for normal steering maneuvers to maintain control and avoid crossing hands.

question: Why shouldn't you follow other cars too closely?
options: a:You may not see the vehicle's turn signals.,b:You may not see the road between cars.,c:You may not have time to stop if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly.
note: Following too closely reduces your stopping time and increases the risk of a rear-end collision if the car ahead stops suddenly.

question: What color are signs that indicate areas of public recreation or cultural interest?
options: a:Orange.,b:Green.,c:Brown.
note: Brown signs indicate cultural, historical, or public recreation areas and are useful for travelers.

question: Which of these does NOT affect your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:The type of alcoholic beverage you drink.,b:How much time passes between drinks.,c:Your body weight.
note: BAC is affected by how much alcohol you drink, your body weight, and the time between drinks; the type of beverage does not change BAC.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before passing another vehicle you should:
options: a:Signal early enough for other drivers to know your plans in advance.,b:Signal after you have changed lanes.,c:Signal just before changing lanes.
note: Signal early enough to give others time to react and avoid surprises when passing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street you should finish the turn into:
options: a:The center of the street.,b:The right lane of the one-way street.,c:The left lane of the one-way street.
note: When turning left onto a one-way street, complete the turn into the lane closest to the one you left (usually the left lane).

question: What are signs called that require drivers to obey indicated instructions?
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Information signs.,c:Warning signs.
note: Regulatory signs (such as speed limits and stop signs) require drivers to obey the instruction shown and violations are punishable.

question: What problems can worn or bald tires cause?
options: a:They improve fuel economy but reduce grip.,b:They only make the ride less comfortable.,c:They can increase stopping distance and make turning more difficult.
note: Tires without adequate tread increase stopping distance, make turning harder, and raise the risk of hydroplaning.

question: Downward-facing triangular traffic signs typically:
options: a:Tell drivers to yield.,b:Indicate construction zones.,c:Indicate a school zone.
note: A downward-pointing triangle is used for yield signs, indicating you should slow and give right-of-way.

question: What color pavement markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Yellow.,b:Both yellow and white.,c:White.
note: Yellow pavement markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions; white markings separate lanes moving in the same direction.

question: Traffic lanes moving in opposite directions are divided by lines of what color?
options: a:Red.,b:White.,c:Yellow.
note: Yellow lines are used to separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

question: In icy or snowy conditions, which of the following choices is most helpful in avoiding a crash?
options: a:Get off the highway as quickly as possible.,b:Engage the four-wheel drive on your vehicle.,c:Add extra weight to your vehicle to improve traction.
note: When roads are snow-covered or icy, the most important strategies are to reduce speed and increase your following distance. Four-wheel drive can help traction but does not replace slowing down and increasing space between vehicles.

question: How can you verify you are stopped at a safe distance behind another vehicle?
options: a:You can see the ground under the other vehicle’s rear wheels.,b:You can read any bumper stickers.,c:You can read the license plate.
note: When you can see the ground under the rear wheels of the vehicle ahead, you have adequate stopping distance to maneuver if needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, which vehicle must yield?
options: a:The car on the left has the right-of-way.,b:The car on the left shall yield to the car on the right.,c:The largest vehicle has the right-of-way.
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously at an uncontrolled intersection, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

question: Why should drivers be extra alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?
options: a:They always disobey traffic laws.,b:They are often harder to see and may have less noticeable lighting.,c:They follow different rules that exempt them from right-of-way laws.
note: Smaller road users can be harder to spot; maintain awareness to prevent collisions.

question: How can you help avoid rear-end collisions?
options: a:Check rearview and blind spots only after braking.,b:Avoid sudden stops and release the gas before braking to slow smoothly.,c:Always brake as hard as possible without warning.
note: Avoid sudden stops by easing off the accelerator to slow before applying steady braking; this gives drivers behind more warning and time to react.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline indicate on a two-lane road?
options: a:Passing is allowed when safe.,b:Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is prohibited.,c:Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is prohibited.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate opposing traffic and indicate that passing is not allowed for either direction.

question: Using which device is associated with a higher risk of driver distraction?
options: a:A cell phone,b:A CD player,c:A radio
note: Using a cell phone (even hands-free) is a significant distraction and increases the risk of a crash; audio devices can also distract but cell phone use is especially hazardous.

question: If a vehicle with ABS loses traction on a slippery road, how should the driver brake?
options: a:Pump the brakes.,b:Press and hold the gas pedal to regain traction.,c:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
note: With ABS, press and hold the brake pedal firmly; the system will automatically modulate braking to prevent wheel lockup.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following statements about passing is true?
options: a:Always wait until you can barely see the passed vehicle before returning to your lane.,b:Use your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot when passing to the left.,c:Signal at least 25 feet before changing lanes to pass.
note: Before passing to the left, signal and check mirrors and the blind spot; do not return to your lane until you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

question: What should be your first response to reduced visibility?
options: a:Turn on windshield wipers.,b:Turn on your headlights.,c:Reduce your speed.
note: The first response to reduced visibility is to slow down; adjust lights and wipers as needed.

question: How is distracted driving best described?
options: a:Extremely risky behavior that endangers the driver and others.,b:A minor concern with little effect on safety.,c:Very uncommon and not a major problem.
note: Distracted driving significantly increases crash risk to drivers, passengers, pedestrians, and cyclists.

question: What does a single broken yellow line down the center of a two-lane road mean?
options: a:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is always prohibited.,b:Lanes move in the same direction and passing is prohibited.,c:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
note: A single dashed yellow line separates opposite-direction traffic and permits passing when safe.

question: If you hear a siren behind you while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to get out of the way.,b:Stop immediately where you are.,c:Pull over to the right and stop to let the emergency vehicle pass.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches from behind, create a clear path by pulling to the right and stopping when it is safe.

question: If you are angry after an incident at work, when you get to your car you should:
options: a:Take a few minutes to cool off before starting your drive home.,b:Drive fast on the interstate to let off steam.,c:Play the radio loudly to drown out thoughts.
note: Distracted or emotional drivers should calm down before driving to avoid making poor decisions.

question: A flashing yellow traffic light means drivers should:
options: a:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.,b:Stop and wait for a green light.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light warns of a hazard; slow down and proceed with caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to change lanes you should:
options: a:Only check your side view mirror.,b:Quickly turn your head to check without using mirrors.,c:Check side and rearview mirrors and quickly glance over your shoulder for other vehicles.
note: Check your mirrors first, then glance over the shoulder in the direction you intend to move to check blind spots.

question: When approaching an emergency vehicle stopped with lights flashing, you must:
options: a:Remain in your lane and keep your current speed.,b:Slow down and,c:Drive to the right side of the road and stop immediately.
note: You must slow down and move over if it is safe to do so to give extra room to emergency, tow, or roadside assistance vehicles; if you cannot move over, slow to a speed below the posted limit.

question: Stop lines painted across traffic lanes indicate:
options: a:Locations next to schools and churches,b:Curves and hills,c:Intersections and pedestrian crosswalks where you must stop.
note: Stop lines are solid white lines at intersections and crosswalks that mark the place where vehicles must stop for traffic signals or signs.

question: If your car begins to skid, where should you steer?
options: a:Keep the front wheels straight.,b:In the opposite direction of the skid.,c:In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
note: Steer into the direction you want to go; as the vehicle straightens, you may need to correct the wheel the other way.

question: Anything that causes you to do which of these could lead to a crash?
options: a:Only take your hands off the wheel.,b:Only take your eyes off the road.,c:Take your attention away from the task of driving.
note: Distractions that remove your attention from driving, your eyes from the road, or your hands from the wheel increase crash risk.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:You do not have to stop when directed to do so by a flagger.,b:It is against the law to go around lowered crossing gates.,c:All railroad crossings are equipped with flashing red signals and gates.
note: You must obey crossing gates and signals; it is illegal to drive around lowered gates, and not all crossings have active warnings.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When the traffic light turns solid yellow as you approach an intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Consider it the same as a caution sign and continue regardless.,b:Speed up to beat the light.,c:Stop before entering the intersection unless you are too close to stop safely.
note: A solid yellow warns that the light is about to turn red; stop if you can do so safely, otherwise proceed cautiously.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The space needed to cross traffic is determined by which factors?
options: a:Road and weather conditions and oncoming traffic.,b:Whether there is a stop sign present.,c:If your turn signal is in use.
note: How much space you need to cross traffic depends on road and weather conditions and the amount of oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes in your direction, which lane should you enter?
options: a:The middle lane regardless of where you came from.,b:The lane marked with an arrow only.,c:The lane closest to your previous lane.
note: When turning into a multi-lane street, enter the lane closest to the one you were in and do not change lanes while turning.

question: If you encounter an aggressive driver you should:
options: a:Avoid eye contact,b:Retaliate by tailgating.,c:Cut them off to slow them down.
note: Remain calm, avoid provoking the aggressive driver, and create distance between you and the threat.

question: Which traffic signal tells you to slow down and proceed with caution through an intersection?
options: a:A solid yellow light,b:A flashing red light,c:A flashing yellow light
note: A flashing yellow traffic light means slow down, proceed with caution, and be prepared to stop if necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended downward, that hand signal means the driver intends to:
options: a:Turn left.,b:Stop.,c:Turn right.
note: A downward extended left arm signals that the driver plans to stop or slow down.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you enter a freeway safely?
options: a:Signal,b:Signal and then accelerate much faster than traffic.,c:Enter slowly; freeway traffic must yield.
note: When merging, signal, yield to existing traffic, and match the speed of vehicles on the freeway to merge safely.

question: When approaching a stopped school bus with its stop arm extended, drivers should:
options: a:Proceed if they think children are finished exiting.,b:Honk before passing on the left.,c:Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.
note: When a school bus displays its stop signal, you must stop and remain stopped until the stop arm is withdrawn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left you must yield the right-of-way to:
options: a:Oncoming traffic.,b:Other drivers already in the intersection only.,c:Pedestrians already in the intersection only.
note: When turning left you must yield to oncoming traffic as well as to pedestrians and others already in the intersection.

question: What do round warning signs usually indicate?
options: a:A no-passing zone.,b:A school zone.,c:An upcoming railroad crossing area.
note: Round signs typically warn of an upcoming railroad crossing; approach with caution.

question: What should you adjust first after getting into a car?
options: a:The steering wheel.,b:Your seat.,c:Your rearview mirror.
note: Adjust your seat first so you can reach controls comfortably and have a clear view of the road, then adjust mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which traffic signal gives you the right-of-way to turn left?
options: a:A green arrow pointing left.,b:A solid green light.,c:A flashing yellow light.
note: A steady green arrow means you may proceed in the direction of the arrow while oncoming traffic is stopped.

question: What does a flashing yellow arrow for left turns allow you to do?
options: a:Merge into the lane in the arrow direction without yielding.,b:Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,c:Come to a complete stop before turning.
note: A flashing yellow arrow permits left turns but requires you to yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.

question: Which practice helps prevent crashes by communicating with others on the road?
options: a:Drive only on side streets to avoid others.,b:Ignore other drivers and focus only on your lane.,c:Signal your intentions and use horn or emergency signals when appropriate.
note: Communicate with other road users by signaling, using emergency signals, or sounding the horn when appropriate to prevent unexpected actions.

question: A properly adjusted lap belt should sit:
options: a:Hidden beneath the seat.,b:Snugly across your hip bones and the lower part of your abdomen.,c:Loosely across your waist.
note: Lap belts should be snug across the hip bones and below the abdomen; shoulder belts should lie comfortably across the chest.

question: Before backing out of a driveway where children are playing, what should you do?
options: a:Sound your horn to warn the children.,b:Rev the engine to get their attention.,c:Exit the vehicle and walk to the back to ensure the way is clear.
note: Do not rely solely on mirrors when children are nearby; get out and check behind the vehicle before backing.

question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:New drivers.,b:Bad weather.,c:Human error.
note: Most crashes occur because drivers make errors—failing to see others or doing something unexpected.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do speed limit signs represent?
options: a:The maximum or minimum legal speed allowed under ideal conditions.,b:Potential driving speeds for the area.,c:A recommended speed only for heavy traffic.
note: Speed limit signs indicate legal maximums (or minimums) for ideal conditions; drivers must slow when conditions require.

question: Combining alcohol with drugs usually causes what effect?
options: a:It decreases the effects of both.,b:It helps cure an illness.,c:It increases the effects of both the drugs and the alcohol.
note: Mixing alcohol and many drugs compounds their effects and can greatly increase impairment, making driving unsafe.

question: Why is it important to be alert for motorcycles?
options: a:They are smaller and harder to see and it is difficult to judge their distance and speed.,b:Motorcyclists are less skilled drivers than others.,c:They rarely use headlights.
note: Motorcycles are harder to see and may be hidden in blind spots; it's also harder to judge their speed and distance so give them extra caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When the center line shows a solid yellow next to a broken yellow and the broken line is next to you, when may you pass?
options: a:Only on expressways.,b:Only in an emergency.,c:When oncoming traffic is clear.
note: If the broken yellow line is next to your lane you may cross it to pass when the way is clear and it is safe to do so.

question: What will help someone overcome the effects of alcoholic drinks?
options: a:Drinking hot coffee.,b:Allowing time for the body to metabolize the alcohol.,c:Getting fresh air.
note: Only the passage of time will allow a person to eliminate the effects of alcohol; coffee or fresh air do not help.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you prepare to make a right turn, your car should be:
options: a:Close to the left side of the street.,b:Near the center of the street.,c:As close to the right side of the road as possible.
note: Position your vehicle near the right edge of the road before making a right turn; do not cross lanes unnecessarily.

question: If another vehicle may hit you, what is an appropriate way to warn them?
options: a:Wave your arms out the window.,b:Use your emergency lights only.,c:Sound your horn to alert the other driver.
note: Use the horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians when you think they may not see you and a collision may occur.

question: As a pedestrian, when should you enter a street or crosswalk?
options: a:Enter at any time because it is the driver's responsibility to stop.,b:Always insist on the right-of-way and step into the crosswalk immediately.,c:Only when it is safe to do so and no vehicles are approaching too closely.
note: Pedestrians should not enter a roadway or crosswalk if vehicles are approaching too closely to allow a safe stop; always ensure it's safe first.

question: A stop sign has the shape of a(n):
options: a:Rectangle.,b:Circle.,c:Octagon.
note: The octagonal shape is used exclusively for stop signs, indicating you must come to a complete stop.

question: When is it acceptable to park in the access aisle next to a reserved handicap parking space?
options: a:When all other parking spaces are full.,b:When you have a handicap plate or placard.,c:Never.
note: Parking in an access aisle is prohibited; misuse is a traffic infraction and punishable by fines.

question: What does a regulatory sign with a red circle and slash indicate?
options: a:The action shown is forbidden.,b:That some drivers must yield to others.,c:Drivers must come to a complete stop.
note: A red circle with a slash across a symbol indicates the specified action is prohibited by law.

question: If your tire suddenly blows out while driving, you should:
options: a:Slam on your brakes immediately.,b:Keep driving at the same speed.,c:Hold the steering wheel firmly and gradually slow to a stop.
note: Grip the wheel firmly, release the accelerator, and slow gradually. Only apply the brakes lightly once the vehicle is moving slowly, then pull to a safe area.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Both must yield and make hand signals.,b:The vehicle on the left.,c:The vehicle on the right.
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching a steady green light, what should a driver do?
options: a:Stop if a police officer is nearby.,b:Treat it like a four-way stop.,c:Proceed if the intersection is clear and yield to pedestrians or vehicles still in the intersection.
note: On a steady green you may continue through if the way is clear but must yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.

question: A person using a white cane or a guide dog is most likely to be:
options: a:A blind person.,b:A deaf person.,c:A person involved with a traffic study.
note: Drivers must always yield the right-of-way to a pedestrian who is blind and using a white cane or guide dog.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a fire engine is following you but not using emergency signals, how should you respond?
options: a:Speed up to get out of its path.,b:Stop immediately to let it pass.,c:Continue driving normally; you do not need to clear the way.
note: When an emergency vehicle behind you is not using lights or siren, continue driving normally.

question: What affects your ability to stop your vehicle?
options: a:The road and weather conditions (road condition).,b:Signal lights.,c:The time of day.
note: Your ability to stop is affected by road conditions, weather, vehicle condition, brakes, tires, and speed; adjust speed accordingly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady green light at an intersection authorize you to do?
options: a:Proceed through the intersection if the road is clear.,b:Must stop and check for oncoming traffic.,c:Always slow and prepare to stop.
note: A steady green means you may go if the intersection is clear, yielding to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.

question: When does your vehicle's stopping distance increase?
options: a:On wet or icy roads.,b:On dry paved highways.,c:Only when driving at night.
note: Stopping distance increases on slippery surfaces such as wet or icy roads and also with higher speeds and poor vehicle condition.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes you should check your blind spots by:
options: a:Turning your head to look over your shoulder.,b:Using only the outside rearview mirror.,c:Using only the inside rearview mirror.
note: Turn your head to check blind spots in addition to using mirrors before every lane change.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do if you arrive at an intersection wanting to turn but are not in the correct lane?
options: a:Quickly cut across traffic to make the turn.,b:Turn on your blinker and turn from your current lane.,c:Drive to the next intersection and make the turn from the proper lane.
note: Do not make last-minute lane changes; continue to the next intersection and turn from the proper lane.

question: If an approaching train is close enough to be a danger, you must:
options: a:Cross the tracks at your own risk.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
note: If a train is close enough to be dangerous, do not cross the tracks; wait until it has passed and all warnings are clear.
